analysis.title: "Quickest Way To Stop The Fed": Hartnett Says Stocks Must Give Up All Of 2026's Gains... And The S&P Is 80 Points Away
key_insights: Hartnett stays risk-off for a sixth straight Flow Show. The S&P closed Friday at 6,925, down 8.4% on the week (worst since Liberation Day) after a seventh straight loss through the 200-day average. The Nasdaq 100 is 19.8% below its October record and the VIX spiked above 39.

Key level: the S&P below 6,845 (2025 close, erasing 2026 gains) plus IG CDX above 80bps would short-circuit the hiking cycle if the Fed still treats stocks as too big to fail. The S&P is about 80 points (1.2%) away.

If the Fed stays tough post-midterms, the March 18 or April 28 FOMC is the earliest markets can price peak rates, and hard-landing risk rises. Tells of peak hike fear are a dollar top and lows in bitcoin, gold and KOSPI. All four currently fail (dollar strongest weekly close since April 2025, bitcoin down seven weeks).

Fed officials show no sign of backing down. Cook said financial conditions are too accommodative, Paulson is open to back-to-back hikes, and the minutes showed almost all officials see more tightening. The 50bps hike Waller wanted is off the table and January hike odds are below 60%.

Positioning has not capitulated. The BofA FMS shows cash at 3.6%, only 3% expecting a hard landing (50% soft, 42% no landing), and a record $310bn into equity funds in four weeks. The Bull & Bear indicator is 7.1 (from 7.4), with equity flows in the 99th percentile and positioning at the 100th.
Goldman Prime shows hedge fund net leverage at a more than five-year low, with the fastest tech selling in a decade. The ETF buyer is holding the bag.

The BofA Global Breadth Rule (net 68% of indices oversold, signal at 88%) likely triggers soon and points to a relief bounce after Thanksgiving. A big rally needs the 10Y below 4.5% (closed 4.91%), WTI below $70 (settled $83.41) and a dollar top (no progress).

The 30Y Treasury is on track for a sixth straight year of negative price returns, the longest streak since 1963-69. Hartnett's biggest fear is that yields rise in the next recession. The note flags tension with his hard-landing playbook of buying bonds.
Soft landing case: the S&P below 7,000 is a buy and breadth recovers in spring (equal-weight S&P 16x, mid-caps 15x, ex-US 12x). Then buy the cyclical Cs: crypto, chips, copper, consumer, condos.

Hartnett's actual view is a hard landing with GDP and EPS cuts. Household stock wealth is fading and hyperscaler capex is forecast at $1.3tn in 2027 (from $822bn in 2026) while free cash flow goes to -$283bn. Confirmation would be jobless claims above 250K and IG spreads above 100bps.

EPS matrix: 7,338 is 18x forward EPS of $408 (16% growth). The S&P at 6,925 is 17.9x on $387 (10% growth). At $370 (5% growth) and 16x the S&P is 5,913. Goldman's Garrett Q4 2018 replay target of 6,294 is 17x $370.

2000 analog: tech peaked, the Fed hiked 100bps, defensives rallied, and in 2001 hikes caused recession. The Nasdaq had twelve bear-market rallies above 10%, so the breadth-rule bounce may not be a bottom.

Flows week to Wednesday: $66.6bn into stocks, $7.4bn out of bonds (first outflow since April 2025), EM debt $7.5bn out (biggest since April 2020), US growth stocks $9.1bn in, tech $5.4bn in for an eighth straight week, crypto -$1.1bn.
YTD scoreboard: oil 44.9%, USD 5.7%, US stocks 4.8%, cash 3.3%, HY -1.2%, IG -3.0%, govt bonds -3.9%, gold -15.1%, bitcoin -29.5%. The dollar has outperformed the S&P in 2026.
FMS year-end 2027 targets: 10Y at 4.9%, EUR/USD 1.12, S&P 7,926, gold $4,341. The 10Y target was hit Friday.
The note's author agrees on the mechanism but thinks the Fed needs more than a flat S&P year, given 67 months of missed target and three hot CPI prints. In 2018 it took a 20% drop.

AI capex boom loop risks becoming a doom loop, with top 10 AI stocks at 38% of the US market.
Hard-landing playbook favors assets negatively correlated with AI: long condos, short chips.

Hartnett says consensus expects more than 15% S&P EPS growth in 2027 and 5-6% nominal GDP, and calls these too high with EPS cuts coming.
Goldman's Oppenheimer pencils in 11% earnings growth for 2027 (forecast).
Nvidia's first print without Jensen was cited as a failed clearing event this week.
